title: How did student chapters start?
headline: Watsi's student chapters started with one student, not with Watsi. Any student can start one.
story: The question comes first, on screen: how did student chapters start? Kimmy tells it: one student, Daniel, learned about Watsi and simply started a chapter himself at Stony Brook. Other students wanted to do the same.

Now chapters run bake sales and fundraising events and choose their patients together. It ends on an open door: it usually takes one person deciding to bring people together. Not a donation ad: no donate button, no urgency.
do: Open on frame 1 with the question typed on screen and Kimmy already on camera.
Then a straight cut into her answer. Question first, answer second.
Keep captions on the whole time, Lato, large. One text at a time.
Name super “Kimmy” only, large, after the question has landed.
Use only her second read, C5064 00:54–02:08.
dont: Don't open on Kimmy saying hello or on a logo.
Don't use the false starts, “sorry” lines or prompter chat. Only the takes named below.
Don't speed-ramp her voice. Trim breaths and pauses instead.
Don't use any of Daniel's interview footage (C5049), and not the “start with one” line. Daniel has his own cut.
